body.x: A software idea only counts once it works, and getting there means defining a problem, choosing technologies, designing a system and building it. A graduation exhibition is where students show all of those steps at once.

The Department of Media Software at Sungkyul University in Anyang is presenting its 2026 Graduation Project Exhibition at COEX in Seoul from Oct. 13 to Oct. 16, during KES 2026, under the theme "Build: Making Ideas Work." Professor Hyeji Yang represents the department. The exhibition features 18 teams, eight in games and ten in web and app development.

Game exhibits include Golmokgil Noliteo, a game designed to support indoor exercise, and Muhanui Durebak, a 2D action-adventure game that incorporates Korean cultural elements. Web and app exhibits include PULSE, a customer-analysis-based promotional platform for independent food-service operators; CLUE, an AI platform that helps users understand, verify and act on policy announcements; and Maeumbom, an AI-powered emotion recognition app tailored to older adults in Korea. Teams show working software alongside the process behind it, from problem definition and technology selection to system design and implementation.

The department teaches virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR), games, and web and app development through project-based, practice-oriented courses. It organizes its curriculum around a framework called CLAPT, for Creative, Liberal, Applicable, Practical and Technology, and three focus areas, VR/AR, Game and APP.

Students from the department have won awards across industry-linked projects, software competitions and academic conferences. They include the Grand Prize at the 2026 industry-linked proof-of-concept (PoC) project presentation hosted by the Gyeonggi Business and Science Accelerator, first place in the student category of the Unreal Challenge "Light and Shadow" and the Grand Prize in the Gabia Website Creation Contest. Academic honors include four Outstanding Paper Awards at the 2026 IPACT domestic conference and three at the 2025 IAAI conference, as well as a Silver Award in the 2025 IAAI CDC Capstone Design Contest.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
